claims.text: The material family of interest is fcc high-entropy alloys derived from the Fe-Co-Ni system.
The primary property targeted for improvement is stacking fault energy and associated magnetic-moment stability.
Stacking fault energy and magnetic-moment stability govern competition between TWIP and TRIP.
Conventional static DFT predicts zero or negligible Cr and Ni magnetic moments in the disordered fcc state.
Static DFT fails to capture significant magnetic-entropy contributions that stabilize the fcc phase and determine finite-temperature SFE.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations induce sizable, temperature-dependent magnetic moments in Co, Cr, and Ni.
At 100 K in fcc CoCrFeMnNi, LSF-derived moments are approximately 0.73 μB for Co, 0.52 μB for Cr, and 0.24 μB for Ni.
LSF-induced moments significantly alter the magnetic-entropy and internal-energy terms of the free energy.
Magneto-volume coupling affects the internal energy and magnetic entropy of the fcc phase.
At low temperatures, magnetic contributions stabilize hcp relative to fcc and produce negative intrinsic stacking fault energy.
As temperature rises, magneto-volume coupling increases SFE and suppresses defect formation.
The mechanism produces a transition from twinning or faulting at low temperature to dislocation glide at higher temperature.
The relevant calculations cover 50–1200 K, include thermal lattice expansion, and represent ambient-pressure fcc conditions.
The fcc Fe-Co-Ni-based system will have an SFE of approximately -15 to 2 mJ m⁻² over 77–293 K.
Negative cryogenic SFE will enhance nanotwin and stacking-fault formation.
The critical temperature for the fcc-to-hcp transition is approximately 430 K.
SFE increases monotonically with temperature and reaches approximately 31 mJ m⁻² at 1000 K.
Omission of explicit phonon effects may account for a predicted transition temperature of about 430 K rather than an experimental value of about 633 K.
The principal current challenge is quantifying orbital and spin contributions well enough to predict fcc-hcp transition and twinning temperatures without explicit phonon coupling.

contradictions.description: The stated scientific challenge concerns orbital-moment contributions, but the proposed mechanism and evidence discuss longitudinal spin fluctuations, spin moments, and magnetic entropy without identifying or quantifying any orbital-moment contribution.
The predicted low-temperature SFE range is stated as -15 to 2 mJ m⁻², which includes positive values, while the falsification rule treats a positive SFE at 77 K as decisive falsification.
